: bactericidal via inhibition of cell wall synthesis (via beta-lactam ring)
•gram (+) coverage, esp. beta-lactamase producing S. aureus
•not active against Enterococcus, MRSA, or gram (-)
: hypersensitivity, GI (N/V/D), neurotoxicity (seizures), acute interstitial nephritis, hematologic (thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, methemoglobinemia)
: bactericidal via inhibition of cell wall synthesis but are intrinsically effective against beta-lactamase producing bacteria
•gram (-) rods (E. coli, H. flu, Proteus mirabilus, Klebsiella)
: allergic reaction (~2% cross reactivity w/ Penicillins)
Unclear on slide (name runs over a petal's edge)
: protein synthesis inhibitor (binds to 30S ribosomal subunit); bacteriostatic
•broad spectrum of activity – good against gram (+), gram (-), atypical organisms, & organisms other than bacteria
•poor GI tolerance: may cause diarrhea & gastritis
•deposition in calcified tissue: deposition in teeth causes teeth discoloration & may affect growth (not usually given in children <8yo for >21d)
•impaired absorption if given w/ dairy products, Ca, Al, Mg, Fe
: cell wall synthesis inhibitor & inhibitor or proteases & other bacterial enzymes; mixture of cyclic peptides that are bactericidal & bacteriostatic
•gram (+) only; little effect against gram (-) & anaerobes
•may be part of triple therapy ointment w/ Neomycin & Polymyxin B
•topical: allergic contact dermatitis – pts w/ allergic reaction to Neomycin may also be sensitive to Bacitracin
•IM: nephrotoxic (so primarily used in topical form)

roles.drugs: Mild or localized impetigo: topical mupirocin 2% for 5–7 days. Topical is as effective as oral or better for nonsevere impetigo
